source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 4 (SB Instructions PDF page 2); line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7

worked: Married filing jointly, both 67 or older (71 and 69): you private pension 60,000; spouse no retirement income; interest 40,000; Social Security 30,000 and 15,000. Both are 67, so the couple may subtract up to 48,000 'regardless of how much retirement income each spouse received': line 16 is 48,000 though all of it is one spouse's. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (you) 60,000.00 + interest 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 38,250.00 (gross 45,000.00; provisional income 100,000.00 + half of 45,000.00 = 122,500.00; taxable Social Security 38,250.00) = 138,250.00. Federal taxable income = 138,250.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 = 103,550.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 138,250.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 138,250.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 138,250.00. Schedule SB: line 4 Social Security adjustment = 38,250.00; line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 71): pension 60,000.00 = 60,000.00; spouse (age 69): none = 0.00; smaller of 60,000.00 and the 48,000.00 cap = 48,000.00; line 50 total 86,250.00. Schedule SB line 17: federal AGI 138,250.00 is not less than 30,000.00, so no 5,000 subtraction. Form 1 line 6 86,250.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 138,250.00 - 86,250.00 = 52,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 52,000 to less than 52,500, column Married filing jointly: 20,355.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 52,000 / 52,500 / 9,636 / 20,355 / 4,244 / 10,158). Line 9 = 52,000.00 - 20,355.00 = 31,645.00. Line 10a 2 x 700 = 1,400.00; line 10b 2 x 250 = 500.00; line 10c 1,900.00. Line 11 taxable income = 31,645.00 - 1,900.00 = 29,745.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule B (joint) as numbers: 3.5% x 19,580.00 = 685.30 + 4.4% x 10,165.00 = 447.26; total 1,132.56, rounded once to 1,132.56. The Tax Table row 29,700 to 29,800 (PDF page 40) gives 1,133; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 1,132.56.
accepted_approximations: The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
